newsitem.title: USA: UAW official blasts GM at strike rally.
newsitem.headline: UAW official blasts GM at strike rally.

text.p: A top United Auto Worker union official blasted General Motors Corp. Tuesday, accusing the nation's largest automaker of corporate greed and not keeping its promises to workers.

UAW Vice President Richard Shoemaker, who heads the union's GM department, spoke at a rally of about 1,200 striking workers and supporters near GM's Pontiac East full-size pickup truck assembly plant.

"They ought to take a dose of the medicine they are trying to force-feed workers," said Shoemaker. "The strikes at General Motors are about corporate greed, about corporate insensitivity and about corporate commitments that are made and not kept."

About 5,800 members of UAW Local 594 struck the Pontiac plant April 22 in a contract dispute. The union wants GM to hire about 600 additional workers to help ease increasing workloads. GM has said it cannot add excess workers if it wants to stay competitive in the global auto industry.

UAW officials said Tuesday no progress has been made in the Pontiac bargaining. Shoemaker told workers the UAW prevailed in its seven-week strike at GM's Oklahoma City, Okla., car plant, despite GM's refusal to acknowledge that it is hiring more than 300 workers at the plant.
"There's absolutely no question about that, and there's no question we will win this strike," he said.
Shoemaker told workers to not listen to Wall Street analysts, who he said are "carrying General Motors' water" and have supported GM's agenda of downsizing and cutting jobs.
Shoemaker also chastised GM for saying the UAW should show restraint as the company tries to cope with labour rates in other parts of the world.
GM's stock fell 12.5 cents to $56.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
